Action Plan:
- Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.
- Arrange urgent in-person evaluation for fever with systemic symptoms at a clinic in central London today, or attend local A&E if this is inconvenient; plan includes immediate malaria testing (thick and thin blood films) and inflammatory markers to identify source of infection.
- Do not allow patient to return to work until this issue is sorted; patient will be seen today so work absence is advised.
- Administrative booking: clinician will draft the plan and contact admin to book an appointment; patient to call the provided number after a few minutes to finalize scheduling.
- Travel-related infectious workup: given recent return from rural Vietnam, prioritize malaria testing and broader infectious etiologies; results will guide urgency and further management.
- Documentation: the clinician will record the diagnostic reasoning and test requests in the consultation notes to present at reception.
- (No COVID-19 vaccine update was noted in the transcript.)

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Fever for ~7 days with night sweats, generalized malaise, myalgias, and nausea; poor oral intake; fatigue.
- Course: Fever with alternating hot/cold periods; modest relief with OTC ibuprofen/paracetamol but persistent symptoms.
- Associated symptoms: Night sweats; musculoskeletal aches; nausea; minimal appetite; headaches (centralized); no cough, sore throat, diarrhoea, or neck stiffness.
- Past medical history: Chronic back pain managed with physiotherapy; no other chronic illnesses reported.
- Medications: Seroxat (paroxetine); over-the-counter ibuprofen and paracetamol (dose/frequency as taken; no documented adverse effects).
- Allergies: Pollen allergy (hay fever).
- Social history: Nurse by profession; non-smoker; moderate alcohol use; regular physical activity.
- Travel history: Recently returned from Vietnam (4 weeks ago); rural exposure with trekking and cycling in farmland; malaria prophylaxis taken (daily regimen with an additional prophylactic). Prophylaxis type not recalled.
- Family history: Father died of heart attack in his sixties (around age 68).
- Vaccinations: Up-to-date (including Hepatitis B and routine vaccines).

Objective:
- No physical examination findings or vital signs documented in the transcript.
- Planned examinations and laboratory tests discussed but not yet performed.

Assessment & Plan:
1) Fever with systemic illness after recent travel (possible malaria)
- Assessment: Malaria is the leading consideration given travel to rural Vietnam and current fever with night sweats and myalgias (high likelihood per DDx). Other plausible travel-related etiologies include leptospirosis, enteric fever/typhoid, dengue, and occult sepsis.
- Differential diagnosis (consistent with transcript/DDx): 
  - Malaria (high likelihood)
  - Leptospirosis (medium)
  - Enteric fever/typhoid (medium)
  - Dengue fever (low)
  - Occult septicemia (medium)
- Investigations planned: Thick and thin malaria blood films; inflammatory markers; additional infectious workup as indicated by exam findings.
- Treatment planned: No empiric antimicrobial therapy started today; symptomatic management with analgesics/antipyretics as needed; plan to tailor therapy after test results.
- Referrals: If FUO persists or malaria is negative/unconfirmed, consider infectious disease consultation and broader FUO workup.

2) Urgent in-person evaluation logistics and test scheduling
- Assessment: Immediate clinic evaluation needed to identify source of fever and determine urgency of malaria/other infections.
- Investigations planned: As above (malaria films, inflammatory markers); scheduling to determine urgency based on exam.
- Treatment planned: To be guided by test results.
- Referrals: Not specified today; dependent on results and clinical course.

3) Work/school clearance and follow-up
- Assessment: Patient advised not to return to work until evaluation and tests are completed.
- Plan: Finalize appointment and ensure timely testing; follow-up with results and clinical decision-making.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing elements to be collected on exam: vital signs and formal physical examination findings (not provided in transcript).
- Missing elements in plan: concrete laboratory results and imaging studies (not yet available); no established final diagnosis at this time.
- Internal conflicts: No conflict between transcript and DDx identified (“conflict noted” not required as none found).
- Transcript quality: Clear overall; some details deferred to in-person examination and testing.

Notes on DDx integration:
- Malaria: Supported as the primary consideration by the DDx (high likelihood). Malaria testing (thick/thin films) specifically indicated.
- Leptospirosis, Enteric fever/typhoid, Dengue: Reasonable differential based on travel/exposure; included with rationale and likelihood from the provided DDx.
- Occult septicemia: Included as a possible cause of fever of unknown origin given systemic symptoms and travel history.
- Drug fever or NSAID-related fever: Considered in DDx but not prioritized absent additional data; no explicit evidence from transcript to support, included as a lower-likelihood consideration in rationale.
- Autoimmune/Still’s disease and endocrine emergencies: Not strongly suggested by current history; included in DDx as less likely considerations in broad FUO workup.

End of note.
